title: Attention Is All You Need
venue: 31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017)
abstract_summary: The paper introduces the Transformer, a novel sequence transduction model architecture that relies entirely on attention mechanisms. By dispensing with recurrence and convolutions, the model achieves significantly higher parallelization during training. It demonstrates superior translation quality on WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French tasks. The model sets a new state-of-the-art BLEU score of 28.4 for English-to-German and 41.8 for English-to-French. Training time is drastically reduced compared to existing state-of-the-art models. The architecture also generalizes effectively to other tasks like English constituency parsing.
problem_and_motivation: Dominant sequence transduction models (like RNNs, LSTMs, and GRUs) rely on complex encoder-decoder structures that process sequences symbol by symbol. This inherent sequential nature prevents parallelization within training examples, which becomes a bottleneck for long sequences where memory constraints limit batching. While attention mechanisms were used in conjunction with recurrent networks to improve performance, the fundamental constraint of sequential computation remained. The authors sought to build a model that avoids recurrence and convolution entirely to maximize parallelization while maintaining or improving translation quality.
contributions: Introduced the Transformer, the first sequence transduction model based entirely on self-attention.
Achieved new state-of-the-art BLEU scores on WMT 2014 English-to-German (28.4) and English-to-French (41.8) translation tasks.
Demonstrated significantly faster training times compared to existing recurrent and convolutional architectures.
Proposed Scaled Dot-Product Attention and Multi-Head Attention as core components.
Introduced a parameter-free sinusoidal positional encoding method.
Showed the model's generalizability to English constituency parsing tasks.

method.overview: The Transformer follows an encoder-decoder architecture using stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully connected layers. The encoder consists of a stack of 6 identical layers, each with two sub-layers: a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a position-wise fully connected feed-forward network. The decoder also has 6 identical layers, with an additional third sub-layer that performs multi-head attention over the encoder output. Residual connections and layer normalization are applied around each sub-layer. The model uses learned embeddings and sinusoidal positional encodings to account for sequence order.

components.name: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
components.description: This is the core attention mechanism. It takes queries, keys, and values as input. The dot product of the query with all keys is computed, divided by the square root of the key dimension (dk) to prevent vanishing gradients, and passed through a softmax function to obtain weights for the values. This allows the model to focus on relevant parts of the input sequence.
components.equations_or_algorithms: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QKT / sqrt(dk)) * V

components.name: Multi-Head Attention
components.description: Instead of a single attention function, the model projects queries, keys, and values h times with different learned linear projections. These projected versions are processed in parallel by the attention function. The resulting outputs are concatenated and projected again to produce final values. This allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.
components.equations_or_algorithms: MultiHead(Q, K, V) = Concat(head1, ..., headh) * WO; where headi = Attention(Q*WQi, K*WKi, V*WVi)

components.name: Position-wise Feed-Forward Networks
components.description: Each layer contains a fully connected feed-forward network applied to each position separately and identically. It consists of two linear transformations with a ReLU activation in between. This is equivalent to two convolutions with kernel size 1.

components.name: Positional Encoding
components.description: Since the model lacks recurrence or convolution, it needs to know the order of tokens. The authors add positional encodings to the input embeddings. They use a fixed sinusoidal function of different frequencies, which allows the model to potentially extrapolate to longer sequences than those seen during training.

method.settings: dmodel=512, dff=2048, h=8, dk=dv=64, N=6 layers. Trained on 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs. Adam optimizer with beta1=0.9, beta2=0.98, epsilon=10^-9. Warmup steps=4000. Label smoothing=0.1. Residual dropout=0.1.

tasks_and_datasets.name: WMT 2014 English-to-German
tasks_and_datasets.description: 4.5 million sentence pairs, byte-pair encoding, 37k vocabulary.

tasks_and_datasets.name: WMT 2014 English-to-French
tasks_and_datasets.description: 36 million sentence pairs, word-piece vocabulary of 32k.

experiments.setup_details: Base models trained for 100k steps (12 hours). Big models trained for 300k steps (3.5 days). Beam search with size 4 and length penalty alpha=0.6.

results.takeaway: Outperforms existing ensembles by over 2 BLEU.
Establishes a new state-of-the-art for single models.

claims_table.claim: Transformer (big) outperforms best existing models on EN-DE
Transformer (big) sets new state-of-the-art on EN-FR

ablations_and_analysis.what_varied: Number of attention heads and head dimensions
ablations_and_analysis.finding: Single-head attention is 0.9 BLEU worse than the best setting; too many heads also hurt quality.
Reducing dk hurts model quality, suggesting compatibility is difficult to learn.
Learned positional embeddings and sinusoidal encodings produce nearly identical results.

limitations: Reduced effective resolution due to averaging attention-weighted positions (counteracted by Multi-Head Attention).
Self-attention complexity is O(n^2 * d), which can be slow for very long sequences.
Determining compatibility with dot-product attention might be less effective than more sophisticated functions for large dk.
failure_modes: Performance drops with too many attention heads.
Performance drops if attention key size (dk) is reduced too much.
Overfitting if dropout is not tuned correctly.
future_work: Apply Transformer to other input/output modalities (images, audio, video).
Investigate restricted (local) attention mechanisms for long sequences.

key_claims.claim: The Transformer is the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention.
The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization than RNNs.

definitions_and_terms.meaning: An attention mechanism relating different positions of a single sequence to compute a representation of the sequence.
A mechanism that performs multiple attention functions in parallel on projected versions of queries, keys, and values.
A model that consumes previously generated symbols as input when generating the next symbol.

related_work_positioning: The paper positions the Transformer against recurrent neural networks (RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs) and convolutional models (ByteNet, ConvS2S). It notes that while attention was previously used, it was almost always in conjunction with recurrent networks. The Transformer is presented as the first model to replace recurrence and convolution entirely with self-attention.

sections_summary.summary: Discusses the limitations of recurrent models regarding parallelization and long-range dependencies, and introduces the Transformer as a purely attention-based architecture.
Reviews existing sequence transduction models (ByteNet, ConvS2S) and self-attention, highlighting the Transformer's novelty in removing recurrence and convolution.
Describes the encoder-decoder stack, multi-head attention, position-wise feed-forward networks, and positional encodings.
Compares self-attention to recurrent and convolutional layers in terms of computational complexity, parallelization, and path length for long-range dependencies.
Details the datasets (WMT 2014), hardware (P100 GPUs), optimizer (Adam), and regularization techniques (dropout, label smoothing).
Presents translation results on WMT 2014 and constituency parsing results, showing state-of-the-art performance.

figures_and_tables.what_it_shows: Comparison of BLEU scores and training costs.
